glance: Fixed. Step 1 of 3, one third of $4,500
From access. Access by Nov 13, results by Nov 20
At no charge, in 30-minute slots, to use however you like

rows.label: Before we start
rows.note: What has to be in place before day 1. My five working days count from signing or access, whichever comes later.

rows.label: Agreement signed and the $1,500 invoice paid
rows.note: Your counsel reviews the agreement first.

rows.get: Your code lives in your own account from day one.
rows.label: A GitHub account in MyAlly's name, with me invited (flashesofbrilliance)
rows.note: Free to set up, about 10 minutes. You can do it before signing.

rows.label: A Lovable invite (zach.harris@gmail.com)
rows.note: So I can link Lovable to your GitHub.

rows.label: No real family or child data
rows.note: I review the rules, not the records. If you'd like me to try the app as a parent, two made-up parent accounts are enough.

rows.label: Code review
rows.note: Is it safe to build on?

rows.label: Read the Lovable code, database rules and build spec
Sort the code into three piles: ready to build on, keep with some tidying, better rebuilt
Write the report

rows.get: The report is yours to keep and share.
rows.label: A short written report, with the reasons for each pile
rows.s2: Shows which screens and flows are solid enough to map the customer journey on.
rows.s3: Decides what the prototype builds on and what gets rebuilt first, so no hours go into code that will be thrown away.

rows.label: Data separation check
Check that each family's data is kept apart in the database rules

rows.get: A list of what is fine, what to fix, and why.
rows.label: Anything risky flagged, in plain language
rows.s2: Tells the design work which information each screen is allowed to show.
rows.s3: Has to pass before any real family uses the prototype, and before the 100-family test.

rows.label: Not part of Step 1: a full security test, or a FERPA, COPPA or HIPAA review
rows.note: This check is a careful read of the code and rules (agreement term 7). A full security test comes later, and legal questions go to a specialist.

rows.label: Your code in your name
Link your GitHub account to Lovable

rows.get: A full history of the code, owned by MyAlly.
rows.label: Every change saved from here on, in your account
rows.s2: Design changes land in the same saved history.
rows.s3: The prototype is built here, and you can hand it to any developer later.

rows.label: Rough numbers
rows.note: Planning estimates for work I would do, not a quote (agreement term 6). If you share them, please share them as my estimates, with the assumptions attached.

rows.label: Start from the AI cost model Morgan and you built, then build the ranges
Write up the ranges and their assumptions
A low-to-high range for a build ready to test with up to 100 families
rows.s2: Firms up in Step 2 into a real range.
rows.s3: Sets the budget the prototype is built against.

rows.label: A range for going from there to a public launch

rows.get: Numbers Kelly can put in the business plan and show funders.
rows.label: Monthly running costs (AI, hosting, security checks) at each stage, over two years
rows.s3: Tells you what the prototype costs to keep running while families test it.

rows.label: Walkthrough and your decision

rows.get: Part of Step 1. It doesn't use your office hours.
rows.label: A 45-minute walkthrough call

rows.get: Stop here and keep everything, or go on at $1,500.
rows.label: Your yes or no on Step 2
rows.note: Nothing later is committed until you say yes in writing.

rows.label: Included at no charge

rows.get: We agree what matters most to you before I read the code.
rows.label: Proposed office hours: 30-minute kickoff
rows.note: Uses 30 minutes of your free office hours. Move or skip it as you like.

rows.get: You hear the early findings and answer my questions, so the report fits how you work.
rows.label: Proposed office hours: 30-minute check-in on what I find in the code
rows.note: Uses 30 minutes of your free office hours. Move or skip it as you like.

rows.get: One-on-one time with me, for any of the topics below.
rows.label: 4 hours of office hours a month at no charge, in 30-minute slots, to use however you like
rows.note: Two 30-minute slots are proposed during Step 1, so 3 hours a month stay free for anything else. Extra hours are $150 an hour, or $125 an hour when booked for 4 weeks or more.

rows.get: About the plan, the app, the families you serve, or how AI fits. No question is too basic.
rows.label: Bring any question, technical or not

rows.get: If anything I deliver is unclear, ask, and I'll walk you through it.
rows.label: Clarifications on the report, the ranges or the agreement

rows.get: I can help you work out what to ask and gather the facts your lawyer will need.
rows.label: Help framing questions for your lawyer
rows.note: What I say is my opinion, not legal advice (agreement term 7). The answers come from your lawyer.

rows.get: Shared on request, as is, for your team to use on MyAlly.
rows.label: Claude skills, plugins and agents from my own working files, for your team
rows.note: I'll suggest the ones that fit how your team works. They stay mine, and you're free to use them for MyAlly (agreement term 5).
rows.s2: Your team can run the same research and writing tools I use.
rows.s3: The same build tools carry into the prototype, so nothing is relearned.

summary: Step 1 of 3 in the MVP Prototype: $1,500 of $4,500, 12 of 36 hours, five working days from access.
title: Step 1: light audit and code review
